title: Look Into the Future: What If the Rules Changed?
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What are you most afraid of losing, and is the fear reasonable?
A student said the author wanted a studio's movie library, so that others couldn't just start a station on their own movies.
I said I would read the author's reasoning.
would either hike our license fees so high that we would no longer have a profitable business

He's looking into the future, I said. This is strategic thinking. And psychologically, fear is driving him. Just like when he was a little kid adapting to different schools. His vision of what could happen is driving him.
Is that fear reasonable? I asked. A student said: yes, the big studios all do it now. I said: his fear was very visionary, because the networks ended up buying the content companies.

groups.heading: Everybody is allowed to use the fiber now

lines.text: I said streaming services now produce their own content, which gives them margins, and also buy content. We no longer have those monopoly practices. Anybody can stream any channel through the modem. It created an enormous amount of wealth. YouTube is a network now.

I asked: who still watches cable? A student said: only for live sports. I said: the market has fragmented. There are so many more choices that it is not consolidated in massive monopolies. There is very little barrier to entry now.

So what does a big company do when a new technology like the internet comes along, I asked? They partner, they joint venture, they acquire, they merge. I gave two examples: a social network buying a photo app because that is where the younger people were, and a search company buying a video site, because people wanted to go right to video.
It's all about keeping them in your little corral, I said, in your little swimming pool of revenue.
What new technology could threaten what you do, and what would you buy, partner with or build?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what your business depends on that someone else controls.
Write the worst thing they could do, like the author's license fees.
Write a technology that could change your market.
Write how big companies in your field protect themselves: partner, acquire, merge.
Write what you could partner with or build now.

check.q: What did I say is driving the author psychologically?
What did I say has happened to the market for channels?
choices: It has fragmented, with very little barrier to entry

check.q: What did I say big companies do when a new technology threatens them?
choices: Partner, joint venture, acquire or merge

recap: Look into the future, and know what you would do if the rules of your market changed.
